title: Consistent global configuration and scripting options
detail: **Missing/partial; specified.** Root options do not provide global `--config`, `--json`, `--non-interactive`, or policy selection. Equivalent controls are scattered among commands.

title: Stable machine-output API
detail: **Partial.** Successful commands often support JSON; failures, envelope/schema, exit details, and event output are inconsistent. F06/F07/F10 demonstrate the consequences.

title: Regression policies for CI
detail: **Partial.** Absolute release gates and compatible run deltas exist. `compare` exits for compatibility/coverage, not a configured degradation in score, latency, or cost. Add predeclared regression tolerances and fail rules.

title: Complete case-result export
detail: **Partial.** Report JSON contains summaries and non-passing evidence. There is no general headless export of every passing/failing case and repetition to JSONL/CSV, with explicit content controls.

title: CI report adapters
detail: **Missing.** Benchmark-result JUnit/SARIF-style exports are absent. The repository's pytest JUnit files are test evidence, not a user feature.

title: Named baselines, tags, and searchable run history
detail: **Partial.** Run IDs, status filters, and a limit exist. Baseline aliases, run tags/notes, metadata search, pagination, and promotion of an approved baseline are missing.

title: Convenient bounded run controls
detail: **Partial.** Plans support selection, repeats, concurrency, retries, timeouts, budgets, caches, and quotas. `run` largely requires editing a plan file. Add validated direct overrides and a dry-run that prints the exact frozen scope.

title: Reproducibility controls and provenance
detail: **Partial.** Selection/bootstrap seeds and frozen configuration exist. The run CLI does not expose the engine's `run_seed`; local source/dependency/commit provenance is incomplete, as F04 shows.

title: Release gates in conversation drafts
detail: **Missing; documented limitation.** Gates can be authored in executable plans but not declared through session draft choices/patches.

title: Retry only failed application work
detail: **Implemented.** `runs retry` creates a bounded child from safe final application failures or explicit parent-scoped cases on finished runs; it rechecks current/frozen policy and dataset/test-world identity

title: Headless run supervision
detail: **Implemented.** **run --detach** and **resume --detach** launch supervised workers with workspace logs; **runs control RUN_ID pause|resume|cancel** and **resume RUN_ID** send sequenced durable requests, offline cancellation finalizes without dispatch, and **runs status** distinguishes the detached process from the current lease owner.

title: Configuration management
detail: **Implemented.** `config show/validate/set` reports effective values and source precedence, validates schemas before atomic edits, and redacts secret-like values. `config profiles add/list/show/use/remove` manages validated per-user provider profiles used by chat and model planning.

title: Structured progress and durable logs
detail: **Implemented.** `run`, `resume`, and `runs retry` support append-only JSONL event logs plus verbosity/quiet controls. `runs events` reads or follows versioned events with cursors. Cross-process log locks protect event order; noninteractive behavior is documented. See `implementation/G13.md`.

title: Warmup and measurement phases
detail: **Implemented.** Bounded plan `warmup_repetitions` and `run --warmup-repetitions`; warmup application calls run before measured calls, consume application budget/quota/cost, bypass cache, produce no metric work, and are excluded from latency and case samples. Reports retain their attempts, spend, and effect-state counts. See `implementation/G14.md`.

title: Richer performance statistics
detail: **Implemented.** Reports and comparisons expose p50/p75/p95/p99, mean and dispersion, retry-inclusive latency, successful-request throughput, and distinct warmup measurements; incomplete timing and unknown phase attribution stay explicit. See implementation/G15.md.

title: Streaming model performance
detail: **Implemented.** Opt-in OpenAI-compatible SSE benchmarking records TTFT, receive-time inter-content-delta intervals, usage-based output tokens/sec, and completion integrity; measured and warmup reports/comparisons expose the summaries. See implementation/G16.md.

title: Segment/slice analysis
detail: **Implemented.** Reports independently summarize application outcomes, latency/streaming, warmups, and metric decisions by group_id or nested case metadata. Output is bounded and respects --no-content; JUnit/SARIF reject the unsupported option. See implementation/G17.md.

title: Dataset utilities and versioned suites
detail: **Partial.** Validation, candidate review/promotion, episodes, content hashes, and schema-aware CSV/JSON/JSONL import now exist. Optional Parquet import requires explicit trust because PyArrow decompresses pages before row-size checks. Dataset diff, deduplication/splitting tools, and a named suite catalog remain missing. See implementation/G18-import.md.

title: Workspace maintenance and portability
detail: **Partial.** Migrations and an artifact GC library exist. CLI backup/restore, portable run/session bundles, workspace integrity/repair, retention/storage usage, and safe GC commands are missing. Absolute recorded paths complicate migration.

title: Judge repeat/calibration workflow
detail: **Partial.** Statistical primitives, native calibration, and comparisons exist. A practical command that repeats/calibrates the configured model judges against reviewed labels is incomplete; F12 affects a helper branch.

title: Platform and release confidence
detail: **Partial.** Windows/Linux CI is configured; macOS CI is absent, current cross-platform results were not observed, and published support/readiness documents still center on older candidates.

title: Advanced scale, load, and modality workflows
detail: **Deferred.** Distributed workers, a scalable work queue, open-loop/ramping load profiles, multimodal evaluators, and a dashboard are product extensions. Ordinary concurrency and RPS quotas already exist.
